title: Protected Main FIFO Interlock Hardening
owner_directive: Make the FIFO queue foundational and durable so lanes cannot force one another through repeated stale-main reconciliation/revalidation.
reproduced_failure: MVPS-08 recorded repeated AIOC main advancement while publication turns were held, causing stale candidates to be yielded, re-reserved, reconciled and revalidated.
That behavior contradicted the intended FIFO invariant that an active turn owns a stable turn_base until merge or explicit yield.
root_cause: FIFO ordering existed in BOOTSTRAP, OPERATING_CONTRACT and ops3_merge_lease.py, but the contract did not state strongly enough that every protected-main writer—including AIOC/control-plane projection and direct contents/ref writes—must participate. Executors could therefore treat FIFO as lane merge etiquette rather than a universal main-write interlock.
implementation: OPERATING_CONTRACT v3.5.0 defines protected-main mutation as a universal repository-local FIFO interlock and prohibits direct protected-main writes.
BOOTSTRAP now states that product, operations/control-plane, checkpoint/CURRENT and compatibility projection writes all participate.
ops3_merge_lease.py exposes validate_protected_main_write and detects direct-main mutation plus held-turn bypass.
Regression tests prove direct writes are rejected, held-turn main advancement is classified as OPS3.PROTECTED_MAIN_BYPASS, and an exact queue-bound PR merge remains the allowed path.
CURRENT truth rules carry the invariant so every lane reconciliation sees it without duplicating queue state.
